# Taskcell

> Taskcell is a self-hosted, open-source (MIT) software factory. Label an issue or move a card, and Taskcell builds it in a sealed Docker sandbox cell, runs your gates and a review, and opens a pull request. You merge. It runs on your machine or server with the AI subscription or API keys you already have.

## How it works

Five steps, the same for every card:

1. **Label**: label an issue on GitHub, GitLab or Linear, or move a card on a GitHub Projects board. A card too vague to build goes back as `needs info` before any model runs. A planner reads the code and writes a tech spec with acceptance criteria, posted on the issue.
2. **Sealed cell**: the agent builds the card in its own Docker container: non-root, no new privileges, minimal capabilities, no repository token, one git worktree per card.
3. **Gates**: your verify script runs and the host scans the diff for secrets. A red gate sends the card back for a repair, at most twice. Then a reviewer reads the diff in a fresh context and fixes what it finds.
4. **Pull request**: the host pushes the branch and opens the PR, ready when every gate passed, a draft when one did not.
5. **Review**: a second model (for example Codex on Claude's work) can review the open pull request read-only and post a verdict (`taskcell review-pr`, or the review workflow in CI). Review comments on GitHub go back for a revision. You merge.

## Setting it up for a user

Follow the setup-taskcell skill: https://taskcell.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/setup-taskcell/SKILL.md (also `.agents/skills/setup-taskcell/SKILL.md` in the repository). It asks where Taskcell should run (this computer, a server for a team, or CI), where the code and tasks are, and which model account, then walks one path with a check after each step.

## Swappable parts

- Sources: GitHub Issues (`--github owner/repo#n`), GitHub Projects (`--source project`), GitLab incl. self-hosted (`--source gitlab`), Linear (`--linear TES-1`).
- Engines: Claude Code (`--provider claude`, default), Codex (`--provider codex`), Cursor (`--provider cursor`), OpenRouter and z.ai (`--provider openrouter`).

## Security

The agent is treated as hostile. The host holds the repository token and the real model key (behind an LLM proxy; the cell gets a one-run nonce), scans every diff for secrets before pushing, and drops agent edits to CI config. The cell can be limited to an egress allowlist. The Hub binds to 127.0.0.1, checks Host headers and needs a per-launch token. No third-party audit yet.

## Keys and cost

Taskcell is free and MIT licensed. It runs on the model plan or keys you already have (Claude subscription, API key, OpenRouter, Codex account); you pay the provider directly and nothing is added.

## Planned, not available yet

Hosting by us is planned and cannot be bought today: Solo (EUR 14 a month), Team (EUR 39), Pro (EUR 79), 20% off when billed yearly, and a 7-day Solo pass (EUR 8). The same plans are priced in US dollars (16, 45, 89 a month; pass 9) and Polish zloty (59, 169, 349; pass 35), and all prices include VAT. The plan is a dedicated server per customer with daily backups and updates done for you, running on your own model keys. The request form on the site is a placeholder and sends nothing.

## Get started

Needs Node 24 and Docker.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/spietrza/taskcell.git
cd taskcell
pnpm install && pnpm build
docker/build.sh          # the sandbox image
pnpm link --global       # puts taskcell on your PATH
taskcell run --github you/app#42 --repo ../app --llm-proxy
```

The CLI is `taskcell`; `vanguard` (the project's former name) still works as a deprecated alias.
